Root cause found: app/web/index.html's ctRank() (Ranked Targets) explicitly passes step:4 to chart_rank_best_per_time, while ctOpenRankAtTime() (Find best target at a specific time) passes no step, defaulting rank_at_time's underlying rank_targets() to step=1. rank_best_per_time's coarse step=4 sweep (needed for performance since it scores every candidate boot time) can land its best-found frame up to step-1 frames from the true local peak, so rank_at_time's finer step=1 search on the same neighborhood finds a strictly better nearby frame -- reading as an inconsistency even though nothing was actually wrong, just imprecise. Fix: new claytonlib/chart/scorer.py refine_near(canon_map, model, initial_time, base_delay, F_center, radius, ...) does a cheap local step=1 search (a few frames either side) scored the same way as rank_targets; app/chart.py's rank_best_per_time now refines each of its top-N returned rows with refine_near(radius=step-1) before returning, re-sorting after. This corrects the REPORTED P(capture) to the true local optimum without paying for a step=1 sweep across the whole window. Added TestRefineNear (3 tests: finds a better frame than a coarse landing spot, never regresses below the starting frame, out-of-range returns None) -- full suite (796) passes. The existing rank_best_per_time round-trip test continues to pass unchanged, exercising the new refine path with real data.

Root cause: sacWidenSeedB() only raised k (frame half-width in sigma units), but app/safari_compass.py's _build_input always defaulted mass_cap=0.999 -- and a k=3.5sigma Gaussian window already covers ~99.95% of its own mass, so mass_cap (not k) was always the binding constraint; raising k barely moved the surviving candidate set (measured: 20434 -> 21162 -> 21163, i.e. saturates almost immediately). claytonlib.compass already had the CORRECT fix for this in its own notebook-facing interactive driver (_prompt_expand: converts a literal frame/second count to k via sigma, then explicitly drops mass_cap) -- the app's stateless seed_b() never adopted it. Fix: new app/safari_compass.expand_window(inputs, add_frames, add_seconds) ports that same (non-interactive) math; _build_input now accepts expand_frames/expand_seconds params and applies it. Root cause: claytonlib.safari_advance.find_in_house_frame's skipped_ambiguous was computed as len(candidates)-len(unambiguous) -- the total count of ambiguous candidates ANYWHERE in the whole search window [current_frame+search_margin, max_frame], with no regard to whether those candidates were actually nearer to the aim than the frame that got chosen. Root-caused via a constructed adversarial repro against the real claytonlib.chart.scorer code (not guessed): rank_boot_marginal's coarse step=4 sweep tracks only the SINGLE best-scoring coarse point per boot time, and refine_near's local search (radius=step-1=3) only ever looks around that one point -- if a narrower/decoy region happens to sit exactly on a coarse grid point while the TRUE higher peak sits further than radius away (very plausible for machete-based criteria, where nearby frames' 50-turn simulation outcomes are essentially uncorrelated, unlike simpler ball-throw criteria), the true peak is invisible to both the coarse sweep AND the narrow refine -- confirmed 0/392 adversarial gap/width combinations passed under the old single-point refine. A full step=1 sweep (matching Mode B's precision) was measured as prohibitively slow at realistic scale (~150s+ for ~3000 candidate boot times, even at the EXISTING step=4) via direct profiling -- capture_probability's own per-call kernel-window cost dominates, not step granularity. Fixed instead by tracking the top-5 (not just top-1) coarse-sampled points per boot time (rank_boot_marginal's new keep_top_k param, claytonlib/chart/scorer.py) and refining around each of them in app.chart.rank_best_per_time, taking the best result -- negligible extra cost (confirmed empirically: no measurable slowdown), and closed 0/392 down to 0 remaining failures across the same adversarial sweep, plus a harder 7-region multi-decoy scenario. Directly answers the user's diagnostic question: yes, 'Rank targets' (Mode A, coarse+refine for performance) and 'Find target at a specific time' (Mode B, always full step=1 for one boot time) are genuinely different algorithms with different precision guarantees -- this narrows but does not mathematically eliminate the gap between them for pathological cases (documented honestly in code comments). fit_safari_offset(per_advance=True) fits intercept AND slope jointly by Theil-Sen (median of pairwise slopes, then median of residuals) over the runs that recorded an advance count, with a seeded percentile-bootstrap 95% CI. fit_safari_offset(jitter=True) estimates safari_jitter_c from the spread of the residuals about whichever fit was actually adopted (line when the gate passed, flat median otherwise), as std/sqrt(mean M) to keep the model's sqrt(M) form. with_safari_offset swaps it in for jitter_c, so safari candidate windows and capture probabilities finally use the spread measured on the SAFARI path instead of inheriting the metronome path's. The no-effect verdicts rest on three properties of the simulation, each now pinned by a test so a change that invalidates one fails loudly instead of silently turning 'cannot matter' into a wrong path: Magikarp only ever uses Splash or Tackle (one bit of RNG, no room for a third move); the user has no burn/poison/paralysis/freeze state at all (only self-inflicted Rest sleep and Rampage confusion); and the battle tracks HP KNOWLEDGE, not HP totals.

15 new tests in tests/test_metronome_abilities.py. One existing assertion updated: test_list_metronome_species expected Granbull to block nothing, which is exactly the behaviour being corrected. 989 tests OK, JS checks clean, nix build OK.

Serene Grace implemented. New BattleContext.secondary_effect_chance doubles the chance (clamped at 100, and 0 stays 0) and effect_proc routes through it -- one site covers the whole ability, because every secondary effect in this battle is the USER's: Magikarp only ever uses Splash or Tackle, neither of which has one.

It shifts the THRESHOLD only. _resolve_proc still rolls exactly once either way, so RNG consumption is unchanged and only the outcome moves -- which was the thing worth confirming, since a change in advance count would have been a much bigger job. Natural Cure verified byte-identical across 400 seeds on both a full movepool and metronome-only.

Magic Guard implemented as an early return in _mark_user_recoil: under it, recoil and crash damage no longer mark the user provably-damaged, so a recovery move fails for want of anything to heal. A failed move skips _POST_METRONOME_SUCCESS_ADVANCES, which desyncs the RNG for every later turn -- so the divergence is real and compounding, not cosmetic.

Deliberately scoped to recoil/crash. Self-inflicted HP costs (Belly Drum, Substitute) are not indirect damage and keep their own marking.

FINDING, and the user called it in advance: at Magikarp level 15 this changes NOTHING across 3,000 seeds, because any Tackle that lands damages the user directly -- which Magic Guard does not prevent -- so recovery succeeds regardless. Below level 15, where Magikarp can only Splash and recoil is the only damage source, it changes 1.35% of paths. Both facts are pinned by tests, including one asserting the L15 no-op so the note fails loudly if it ever goes stale.
